chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:
"If a man eats from the sacrificial animal (Hady) voluntarily, there is nothing upon him; and if it was obligatory, then upon him is the value of what he ate."
And there is no harm in eating the meat of the sacrificial animals after the three days and storing it. He narrated.

key_terms.اَلثَّلاَثَةِ اَلْأَيَّامِ: The three days (of Qurr in Mina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating Hajj sacrificial meat voluntarily or if it was obligatory?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the distinction between voluntary and obligatory Hady, establishing that voluntary consumption incurs no penalty while obligatory cases require paying the value of the meat consumed. It further validates the practice of storing and consuming sacrificial meat beyond the initial three days of Qurr, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the distribution and preservation of Udhiyah.
